item.title: Meridian police officers recognized at inaugural awards ceremony
item.description: Law enforcement and officials from Meridian, Lauderdale County and the surrounding area took time Wednesday to recognize several Meridian police officers for their service to the community at Meridian Police Department’s inaugural awards ceremony at the Frank Cochran Center.

item.title: Scouting America councils merge to form Mississippi Riverlands Council
item.description: The Andrew Jackson Council, based in Flowood, and the Choctaw Area Council in Meridian, have approved the merger following a yearlong review and planning process.

item.title: Ode to a turkey vest
item.description: It was one of the “must have” items at this year’s NWTF Convention according to the hot-off-the-presses article I read prior to entering the exhibit hall and, as a result, now standing slack-jawed while surveying row upon row of exhibitors and gear, I added a stop at the Chêne booth to my list of destinations.

item.title: Supervisors consider waiving second quote on heavy equipment repairs
item.description: Lauderdale County supervisors are considering measures to cut costs and speed up repairs of heavy equipment. The Board of Supervisors is expected to vote Monday on a measure to waive the need for two quotes in some cases.

item.title: Local students serve as Senate pages
item.description: Five local students recently served as pages for the Mississippi State Senate, where they ran errands for state officials and Senate staff. Serving as pages were Asher Boles, Shelby Kate Clark, Madison Harbour and Sam Hines of Meridian, as well as Lauren Skinner from Little Rock.

item.title: Meridian leaders unveil Mississippi Freedom Trail marker in African American Business District
item.description: Meridian’s African American Business District was once a thriving spot for Black residents to shop, mingle and have fun. On Friday, local leaders took time to remember that history and call for its preservation as the Mississippi Freedom Trail unveiled a Meridian Movement monument in the historic neighborhood.
